name: did-we-drift
description: Project-drift audit for agent-built software. Grades two axes separately: the WORK (ON TRACK / DRIFTED (MINOR|MATERIAL|CAPTURED) / INCONCLUSIVE / BLOCKED) and the BASIS it was measured against (RATIFIED / PROVISIONAL / NONE), so a real-but-scattered plan gets a usable verdict instead of a refusal. Classifies every candidate goal USER-RATIFIED / UNKNOWN / AGENT-DRAFTED on mechanical git evidence, catching the common trap where a user asks an agent to write the directive that governs the build and no human-authored scope ever exists. Basis recovery for projects that never wrote a plan: reconstructs candidate goals from declared intent — never from code — and a ratified sentence governs FORWARD from its own date, so prior work is reconciled, never retroactively graded. Refuses to certify on-track without an enumerable work map. Grade-gated drift interrupts with plain-English consequence scenarios, snooze-with-memory, transactional repair, pointer-only resume prompts, and run-to-plan binding for /loop and /goal sprints. QUICK single-agent audit by default; contamination-scaled DEEP fan-out when triggers fire.
